# Liquid Glass Studio

Repository: https://github.com/iyinchao/liquid-glass-studio
Pinned revision: `f7b28c36305a862f5cffed3ddd51511cf1204f56` (MIT, iyinchao).

`shaders/` and `shaders-wgsl/` are the unmodified shader sources from this revision. `LICENSE`, `README.upstream.md`, and `package.upstream.json` preserve the upstream attribution. This directory is independent of the older `vendor/lens` project.

`glass/unified-shader.ts` imports the original GLSL SDF and extracts the normal, Fresnel and directional-glare calculations from production step 9. The adapter replaces the demo's two hard-coded shapes with a bounded group of registered DOM rectangles and uses Studio's smooth minimum for the lighting field. It has no background sampler, refraction, dispersion, tint fill or opaque interior. The original complete GLSL/WGSL optics remain intact as source reference; only this transparent lighting subset is active.

Each local group has separate outer-surface and inner-detail lighting fields, so a containing menu/track does not swallow the selected-row/thumb lighting. Local adaptations normalize compact-control normals and clamp the Fresnel/glare `pow` base before exponentiation. Native rdev/CSS filtering exclusively samples the actual browser backdrop. This lighting SDF fusion is not complete fused background refraction, and it does not reproduce Studio's full background optical pipeline.

`unified-scene.ts` now reserves at most four permanently local WebGL2 lighting canvases: two steady moving-lens groups (indicator/thumb) and two transient menu/highlight groups. Ordinary buttons/toolbars retain continuous native glint/shadow and cannot consume the moving-lens slots. Each canvas has at most 49,152 backing pixels (196,608 in total). Admission is structural for its mounted lifetime, never hover/focus priority; canvases are never reparented. The structural size check includes the full 52 by 68 CSS-pixel overscan of free lenses, so an oversized group cannot occupy a lighting reservation. This replaces the former one-context DOM-raster ownership system. The lighting envelope is bounded by the actual viewport and ancestor scroll clips. Its later sibling slot has a fixed zero-area layout box; only its child canvas uses that expanded envelope. `contain:layout style` with `overflow:visible` treats the child's extension as decorative ink under [CSS layout containment](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#layout-containment), so the lighting cannot expand form scroll geometry. Native lens ancestors receive no clip/mask/filter/opacity from this adapter. A shared native controller supplies pointer, pressure, bend and velocity. There are no background textures/captures, idle frame ticker, or duplicated GPU shadows. The actual appearance and hardware performance require human runtime assessment.
